title: Auto Loans: Returned Payments
content:
When the paying bank sends an Auto Loans payment back unpaid, Piedmont Crescent Bank unwinds that payment completely and charges a returned payment fee. This page sets out what unwinding means.

## Input, judgement and output

| Part of the returned payment | What happens when it is reversed |
|---|---|
| Principal share | added back to the loan's unpaid principal by a payment reversal |
| Interest share | becomes accrued interest again, because the last payment date goes back to the date it carried before that payment |
| Fee share, if any | falls due again as one fee coded as a settlement reversal, naming the returned payment as its related entry |
| The installment it had satisfied | is treated as unpaid once more, which means a late charge may arise when the grace days run out |

## Returned payment fee

The return itself brings a returned payment fee of the product's amount, booked as a returned payment fee that names the returned payment. A single returned payment never carries more than one such fee; an existing one is identified from the loan's activity by the returned payment it names.

## Outside this policy

Deciding to block a payment source after repeated returns belongs to fraud operations and is not governed here.

## Illustration (hypothetical payment)

A payment of 450.00 that had been split as 25.00 to fees, 110.00 to interest and 315.00 to principal is returned. Principal rises by 315.00; the 110.00 of interest is owed again because accrual restarts from the earlier last payment date; 25.00 falls due again as a settlement reversal; and a returned payment fee is added. The installment that payment had satisfied is open again.
